description_full: FRP Holdings, Inc. engages in the real estate business in the United States. The company operates through four segments: Industrial and Commercial, Mining Royalty Lands, Development, and Multifamily. Its Industrial and Commercial segment owns, leases, and manages commercial properties. The Mining Royalty Lands segment owns, leases, and manages mining royalties in Florida, Georgia, and Virginia. Its Development segment owns and assesses the use of parcels of land that are in various stages of development; and constructs new buildings own and operate. The Multifamily segment owns, leases, and manages buildings through joint ventures. FRP Holdings, Inc. was founded in 1988 and is based in Jacksonville, Florida.

financial_summary: FRP Holdings, Inc. is a small-cap real estate business with a $358M market cap on $43M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years and +2% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 1% against a 6% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 39%.
The company is burning through $21M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 10.5× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.1%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 40% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
